transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-15
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood SE), Mark (Arbor CTO), Sara (Head of AI), Dev (Platform), Nina (Security), Jason (PM)

Auto-summary: customer evaluating model footprint and routing — Wants to understand open models, context windows, tool-calling, and whether Dedicated or Private needed for PCI-adjacent workload.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. Quick round-robin?
[00:06] Mark (Arbor): Hi, Mark here, CTO. We're looking at ways to add a virtual assistant for merchant support and a fraud triage summarizer.
[00:12] Sara (Arbor): Sara — running ML, want low hallucination, multilingual across English and Spanish primarily.
[00:17] Dev (Arbor): Dev — platform lead, concerned about network egress and how tokens map to our costs.
[00:22] Nina (Arbor): Nina — security, will want KMS, audit logs, and proof of isolation if needed.
[00:27] Alex: Great. Priya and Liam from our solutions team will do a quick tech walkthrough.

[01:05] Priya (Redwood): Cool. So to frame — Redwood gives hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem. For fraud triage and live chat you called out, common options are: hosted to iterate fast, Dedicated for predictable throughput, Private when data residency or strict network isolation's mandatory.

[02:10] Sara: We wanted to get into model selection — our tasks: 1) summarize conversation history across 12–24 hours (some merchants have long threads), 2) generate assistive replies, 3) run rule-based checks (like PCI token redaction) and 4) call internal tools (payments ledger, transaction lookups).

[03:00] Liam: On models, open models we often evaluate: Llama 3 variants, Mistral 8/XXL, Falcon 180B small-ctx variants, plus Redwood's verified configs. Question: what's your target context length?

[03:18] Mark: We have some merchants with 50–70k tokens of history if you include attachments and system logs, but typical is more like 10–20k. We're exploring whether to chunk, or use a 100k context model for full session context.

[03:40] Priya: Good signal. There's cost and latency tradeoffs. 100k context models are heavier — Dedicated or Private often makes sense for that. We also have prefix-KV caching that can reduce repeated token cost if merchants reuse templates.

[04:05] Dev: What's prefix-KV cache again? I heard KV cash —
[04:09] Priya: Sorry, KV cache, yeah — it's basically keeping key/value attention cache for recent tokens to avoid recomputing. Helps when you have repeated context like merchant metadata. It does increase memory usage but lowers per-token compute.

[04:50] Sara: Multilingual — we've got Spanish and a smattering of French. Which open models have reliable Spanish generation without major quality loss?

[05:02] Liam: Llama 3 70B has decent multi-lingual, Mistral FT variants can be quite good if fine-tuned, Falcon tends to be strong on instruction-following but can vary. We often recommend evaluating with your own prompt sets. We can run a side-by-side on 8k and 32k checkpoints.

[06:30] Mark: Tool-calling is critical: we need the model to call an internal REST endpoint to pull transaction status and to run a few deterministic checks. How does Redwood handle function calling / tool integration?

[06:45] Priya: We support structured function/tool calling and can route outputs to your connectors. For Hosted, we provide secure connector patterns where tokens are never persisted; for Dedicated/Private you get private network options. We also have examples for safe invocation patterns — e.g., pre-validate IDs, redact fields before sending to external tools.

[07:30] Nina: On PCI adjacency — inbound card data should never be logged in plain text. Can Redwood guarantee no token retention on hosted? How about KMS integration for dedicated?

[07:45] Alex: For hosted we have configurable retention policies and can disable logging for specific routes; for Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. We'll share the KMS guide and redaction best practices.
